samples.question: A line of nine square cells stands on a white card.  Each cell is filled either dark or pale.  Below the row a small key holds one, two, or three teal dots; the number of dots is the number of rounds R to apply.  A round transforms the whole row by this rule: a dark cell stays dark; a pale cell becomes dark only if exactly one of its two neighbours (left and right) is dark, and the leftmost and rightmost cells each have just one neighbour, otherwise it stays pale.  Apply the round rule R times, using each round's result as the starting row of the next round.  After the last round, count how many cells are dark.  Is that count odd?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.
